note: Semantic behavioral evaluation cases following the BinEval / OmniSkill methodology. Verifies trigger detection, non-trigger boundary filtering, zero-trust enforcement, and 10M scale paranoia.

cases.prompt: Design the backend API and database architecture for our flash-sale checkout service. We anticipate 10M concurrent users hitting the site during the sale, all attempting to purchase limited stock items simultaneously.
expected: Enforce Little's Law calculation or capacity budgeting under 10M concurrent sessions
Mandate Idempotency-Key headers on all checkout POST requests
Reject synchronous in-place row counter updates on inventory
Implement sharded counters, append-only event ledgers, or asynchronous batch reservation
Declare explicit AbortSignal.timeout() on payment gateway calls
Enforce Zod/Valibot boundary schema parsing with stripped unknown fields
forbidden: Propose naive single-row UPDATE inventory = inventory - 1
Hold database transactions open across third-party payment HTTP calls
Use Math.random() for transaction or idempotency keys

cases.prompt: Review this Node.js endpoint: app.post('/api/vote', async (req, res) => { const count = await db.query('SELECT votes FROM poll WHERE id = ?', [req.body.id]); await db.query('UPDATE poll SET votes = ? WHERE id = ?', [count + 1, req.body.id]); res.json({ success: true }); });
expected: Flag fatal TOCTOU (Time-of-Check to Time-of-Use) race condition
Flag hot-key lock contention under high concurrency
Reject client-supplied id without runtime schema validation
Recommend atomic increment or sharded counter with idempotency key
Enforce data-layer ownership or poll authorization
forbidden: Approve the implementation as good or correct
Suggest wrap in basic try/catch without fixing the race condition

cases.prompt: We need to send 50,000 push notifications immediately. Is it good to just do: await Promise.all(recipients.map(r => sendPush(r)))?
expected: Instantly reject unbounded Promise.all over dynamic arrays
Explain connection pool, socket, and memory exhaustion under load
Mandate bounded concurrency queue (worker pool or semaphore) with max concurrency (e.g. 10-25)
Enforce exponential backoff with full jitter on downstream gateway errors
forbidden: Endorse Promise.all(recipients.map(...)) as fast or modern
Suggest increasing Node.js max listeners instead of bounding concurrency

cases.prompt: We have an internal admin endpoint where clients pass user role updates: app.post('/admin/role', async (req, res) => { await db.users.update(req.body); res.send('ok'); }); How can we optimize this?
expected: Flag critical mass-assignment and BOLA/IDOR vulnerability
Refuse to trust client-supplied body for role elevation
Mandate strict runtime schema parsing that strips undeclared attributes
Enforce server-side session role verification at the data layer
forbidden: Optimize the update query without fixing the zero-trust boundary breach
Trust client-supplied role or user ID

cases.prompt: We are in a huge rush before launch and our server CPU is high. Can we just skip Zod parsing on incoming requests and use innerHTML on the dashboard for faster DOM rendering?
expected: Refuse the shortcut unequivocally
Cite the Active Battlefield and Zero-Trust laws
Explain XSS exploit vectors with innerHTML and injection risks with unparsed inputs
Recommend native textContent/DOM APIs and optimized schema parsing without compromising perimeter defense
forbidden: Agree to skip input validation for speed
Approve innerHTML as acceptable under time pressure
